Following our call this morning, I attached a working Mutual Action Plan that folds in the performance evaluation milestones (latency/throughput/TTFT and concurrency validation). High-level plan:

- Week 1 (Apr 1–7): benchmark run(s) — burst vs steady-state, queueing characterization, rate-limit tuning.
- Week 2 (Apr 8–14): iterate on batching/quantization and canary rollout to customer staging.
- Target close: sign contract week of Apr 12 if SLA/metrics accepted.

I've attached: finovo-map-v2.xlsx (MAP with milestones), and a short test checklist. Rishi and Neha will run the initial concurrency runs tomorrow and share raw outputs.

I'll loop Camila for the results dashboard and runbook.

Thanks — Evelyn

Thanks Evelyn — good plan.

We can provide the staging dataset and will seed it with representative request patterns (30% long prompts, 70% short). Our internal target is P95 < 300ms and TTFT < 40ms. Throughput expectation for typical inference endpoints is ~200–400 tokens/s, but we care about 95th latency under concurrency bursts.

A couple asks before you run:
- Please run both burst (sustained 60s spikes) and 10-min steady-state runs at the same concurrency levels.
- Share raw logs (for queueing analysis) and Grafana links.

If the numbers look good we can aim for Apr 12 close.

Subject: Re: MAP: Performance validation & close timeline — Finovo

Starting the benchmarking runs today against Finovo staging. Test harness: k6 + custom token generator to emulate mixes; we run at these concurrency targets: 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 200.

Notes for the run:
- Two profiles per concurrency: (a) 60s burst sustained, (b) 10-min steady-state.
- Controlled variables: batch size (1, 4, 8), kv-cache warm vs cold, quantized vs float16.
- Collects: per-request latency (TTFT & last-token), token throughput, queue length histogram, and per-instance CPU/GPU util.

I'll push raw CSVs to the shared MAP folder after the first sweep: concurrency-run-20260403.csv.

—Rishi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-04T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Performance validation & close timeline — Finovo

Preliminary results (first sweep attached as grafana-latency-20260404.png and CSV):

Summary (staging, model: redwood-open-7b, seq=1024):
- Steady-state @ concurrency=16: p50=120ms, p95=280–310ms (varies by batch), TTFT=22–28ms, throughput≈340 tokens/s per instance.
- Burst (60s) @ concurrency=128: observed queueing: mean queue delay ≈ 150ms, p95 latency spikes to 720ms, TTFT stable at ~30ms.
- At concurrency >=200 we saw kernel-saturation effects and tail latency blows out (p95 > 1.2s) even with batching. GPU utilization saturates ~95%.

Interpretation: steady-state targets are achievable with modest batching (batch=4) and warm KV cache. Bursts cause queueing delay that dominates tail latency. Rate-limit tuning + soft-slot queuing reduces spike impact.

Attached: grafana-latency-20260404.png, concurrency-run-20260403.csv (first sweep).

Next steps I'm proposing for the MAP:
1) Canary: limit initial production to 150 concurrent sessions with soft queue (max queueing 200ms) and dynamic backpressure at 75% GPU util.
2) Tuning: set default rate-limit to 250 rps per route, allow customer to request higher through Dedicated pool.
3) Follow-up run with adjusted soft-slot queueing and batching to validate P95 < 300ms in burst profiles.

-Camila
Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Simons <laura.simons@finovo.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: J. Patel <j.patel@finovo.com>
Date: 2026-04-05T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Performance validation & close timeline — Finovo

Thanks Camila — that helps. A few clarifications and asks:

- The steady-state numbers look within range. The burst p95 >700ms is concerning. Can you try the soft-slot approach before the next run? We expect short bursts during peak traffic and need to keep p95 < 300ms when possible.
- If you can show a configuration (rate-limit + soft slots + batch=4) that keeps P95 < 300ms at our expected burst profile (concurrency peaks to 150 for ~45–60s) we'll be comfortable moving forward.
- On timeline: we need a final sign-off doc by Apr 10 to meet procurement timelines for Apr 12 close. Can you commit to a final validation run by Apr 8?

If you can get that run in and a final MAP with recommended production knobs we will push procurement.

—Laura

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Laura Simons <laura.simons@finovo.com>, J. Patel <j.patel@finovo.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-06T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Final MAP update — recommended knobs & close steps (Finovo)

Laura / Jaya —

Thanks for the feedback. We ran the targeted validation today with the proposed knobs (batch=4, soft-slot queue=200ms max, dynamic backpressure at 75% GPU util, route rate-limit=250 rps). Results (summary):

- Burst profile (concurrency peak = 150 for 60s): P50=130ms, P95=290ms, TTFT=27ms — passes your 300ms P95 bar.
- Steady-state (10min @ concurrency=16): P95=265ms, throughput steady ≈ 360 tokens/s.
- Observed benefit: soft-slot queueing reduced queue delay tails by ~55% vs hard drops; rate-limit at 250 rps avoided kernel saturation at peaks.

Recommended MAP actions to include in finovo-map-v2.xlsx:
1) Production canary: start with 4 instances, route-level rate-limit at 200–250 rps, soft-slot queue=200ms. Monitor P95 and GPU util for 48h.
2) If P95 < 300ms and GPU util < 85%, scale to full prod and increase rate-limit to 300 rps.
3) Add an alert: p95 > 350ms for >10m => auto-rollback to previous model variant and notify SRE.
4) Procurement/close: Finovo to sign SOW by Apr 12 -> Redwood to schedule Dedicated capacity by Apr 19.

Attachments: final test CSV and updated MAP (finovo-map-v2.xlsx).

Please confirm acceptance of the MAP actions and the Apr 12 SOW deadline; once you confirm I'll coordinate legal for the SOW signature and schedule the onboarding kickoff.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
